key_messages: A cold front will bring widespread showers to the region this morning into the early afternoon, with temperatures falling behind the front. Crisp, dry, and beautiful, fall weather will follow for the weekend.
A quick moving cold front will bring showers Sunday night into Monday with sharply colder temperatures.
A push of cold air will likely result in some frost/freeze midweek, and then moderating as we approach next weekend.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
506 AM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 505 AM EDT Friday...

The Lake Wind Advisory for Lake Champlain has ended.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 223 AM EDT Friday...

1. A cold front will bring widespread showers to the region 
this morning into the early afternoon, with temperatures falling 
behind the front. Crisp, dry, and beautiful, fall weather will 
follow for the weekend.

2. A quick moving cold front will bring showers Sunday night 
into Monday with sharply colder temperatures.

3. A push of cold air will likely result in some frost/freeze 
midweek, and then moderating as we approach next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 223 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 water vapor depicts a good stream of sub-
tropical moisture extending from SW Quebec to SE Texas along an 
elongated longwave trough. Radar shows scattered rain showers moving 
into the St. Lawrence Valley from the southwest with steadier rain 
to follow, currently over the southern Great Lakes. A surface cold 
front will continue to shift precipitation east by daybreak across 
northern New York and the Champlain Valley. Moisture associated with 
this system continues to anomalously high given PWs around 1.5-1.7 
inches, however, an associated LLJ to 40-50 knots will keep the 
moisture corridor progressive, precluding any flooding threats. That 
said, some downpours from more moderate rain will be possible, 
especially across the Adirondacks around sunrise. The front 
continues to track east by midday today, with showers tapering off 
across much of the region after 2 PM. A secondary front will follow 
the main cold front this afternoon, clearing the region of any 
lingering shower activity and drying the region out. Along this 
secondary front, some convergent flow may allow for some lingering 
isolated showers across southern Vermont and along the central 
Greens, but all areas will see a drying trend by this evening. Total 
rainfall will be between a quarter to half an inch, focused mainly 
in northern New York and along the spine of the northern Greens. 
Good shadowing form the Adirondacks and Greens, may lead to lower 
amounts in the Champlain Valley, and especially in southeastern 
Vermont. Temperatures today will be tricky with how fast the front 
moves through. Many locations will generally stay in the low to mid 
60s, however, areas in southeastern Vermont, like Springfield could 
break into the low to mid 70s with a delayed arrival of the front 
and associated precipitation. 

Cloud cover will decrease quickly overnight tonight as drier 
northwest air advects into the region. Temperatures will cool into 
the 40s across the area, with a few pocket upper 30s possible in the 
Adirondacks. By Saturday, a picture perfect fall day is expected. 
High temperatures will be crisp in the mid 50s to around 60, with 
little wind outside of some light channeled north winds in the 
Champlain Valley. High pressure will move overhead Saturday night, 
so expect a chilly Saturday night with temperatures in the mid 20s 
to low 30s in the Adirondacks and NEK, to the upper 30s in the 
Champlain Valley and southern Vermont. Winds will turn southerly 
Sunday, bringing some warmer air as highs warm into the low to mid 
60s. Clouds will also be on the increase Sunday afternoon, though no 
rain is anticipated during the daylight hours through Sunday 
evening. It should be a perfect weekend for leaf peeping, so hope 
everyone can get out and enjoy the foliage!

KEY MESSAGE 2: Our next chance for showers across the area will be 
Sunday night into Monday as a surface cold front passes through. Our 
flow pattern will amplify by the end of the weekend as a pair of 
systems moves through the eastern CONUS. An area of southern stream 
energy will remain shunted south, keeping the more moisture-rich air 
to our south Sunday. However, an area of northern stream energy 
associated with an occluding upper low over the Hudson Bay of Canada 
will glance the region with showers possible Sunday night. As the 
upper low occludes over northern Quebec, it will drag a surface cold 
front more north as well. As such, better precipitation chances look 
to be across our northern zones, and areas closer to the 
International Border. A tightening pressure gradient will also lead 
to a fairly strong 40-50kt LLJ Sunday into Monday, resulting in some 
gusty winds Sunday Night into Monday. Soundings support localized 
gusts in the Champlain and St. Lawrence Valley between 25-30 MPH. 
Behind the front, our air mass will turn more cold and drier, with 
sharply falling temperatures under strong caa. Highs Monday will 
only be in the low to mid 50s.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A vigorous upper low will shift the 1000-500mb 540 dam 
thickness line south of our forecast area. A sharp front will shift 
east with marginal moisture on Monday. It still may be capable of 
developing a solid, narrow line of rain given the vigorous forcing. 
Behind this front will be an impressive push of cold air tamping 
temperatures down into the 50s, except some 60s in the Upper Valley. 
Strong northwest flow will advect plenty of cold air Monday night 
into Tuesday, with widespread mid 20s to mid 30s, though areas near 
Lake Champlain will likely hover around 40. There should be some 
level of flow lingering into Monday night into Tuesday that should 
keep frost from developing. Of course, several places will simply go 
straight to freezing. Fall will very much be in the air on 
Tuesday with brisk winds and high temperatures lingering in the 
mid 40s to mid 50s. Then on Tuesday night, broad surface high 
pressure will set up overnight. It looks like we'll also be 
around the PWAT min across the region, and so very efficient 
radiational cooling is possible. Almost the entire region could 
experience a freeze, and the Champlain Valley remains in the 
alert window for this time. So this will likely be curtain call 
for all gardener's sensitive plants in the broad valleys for 
Tuesday night. Surface high pressure will amble east after 
Wednesday, and temperatures will start moderating. The next 
front will arrive next Friday with some scattered light showers.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 06Z Saturday...Rain is quickly shifting southwest to
northeast ahead of a frontal boundary. This rain is moving in
quickly in part due to fast flow aloft, including 40-45 knot
southwest winds still at 2000 ft agl. Several terminals have LLWS
noted for the next several hours, along with PROB30s and VCSH for
scattered showers. Ceilings at KSLK, KMSS, and KEFK are already
trending downwards toward MVFR, but the rest of our area has
ceilings at or above 5000 ft agl. As the front approaches, rain will
become more widespread with moderate rates moving visibility to
3-5SM, locally to 2SM around 10z-15z in northern New York and about
13z-17z for Vermont. Ceilings at KSLK, KMSS, and KEFK could spend
some time around 700 ft agl, but most areas will trend 1500-2500 ft
agl. The activity will likely decay across Vermont. So reductions to
ceiling and visibility will likely be less drastic. Winds will
switch from south to southwest, and then go northwest behind the
boundary. Ceilings will slowly improve behind the front, but most
areas should be VFR by 00z Saturday as skies clear.

Outlook...

Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
